caseno: First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 340 of 2023 with Civil Rule No. 777 (FM) of 2023.
lawyer:
Amit Das Gupta, Advocate—For the Appellants. 
Rafiqul Islam, Advocate with Rasida Chowdhury, Advocate—For Respondent Nos. 1 -4.
parties:
Badal Akond (Md) and others -------- Appellants
VS
Abdul Maleque and others -------- Respondents
full_judgment:
The above mentioned First Miscellaneous Appeal is directed against judgment and order dated 3-4-2023 passed by Learned Divisional Special Judge and Special District Judge, Barishal dismissing Miscellaneous Case No.1 of 2020 filed under Order XLI, rule 19 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 4. The present appellants as petitioners filed Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 2020 on 6-7-2020 under Order XLI, rule 19 of the Court of Civil Procedure for readmission of the appeal causing delay of 307 days contending, inter-alia, that the tadbirkar as well as appellant No. 1 became seriously ill and bedridden and after some recovery came to the serestha of the learned Advocate on 25-3-2020 and learnt that the appeal was dismissed for default on 26-8-2019. They also filed an application under section 5 of the Limitation Act for condonation of delay on the ground that due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the Civil Courts were closed and the appellants could not file the application in time and, as such, the delay in filing the miscellaneous case should be condoned. Respondent Nos. 1-4 filed written objection contending that before dismissal of the appeal the appellants were not diligent to conduct the appeal and did not take any steps for hearing and there was serious latches and negligent on the part of the appellants in conducting the appeal and, as such, the miscellaneous case should be dismissed. The Court of appeal, after hearing the parties, vide order dated 3-4-2023 dismissed the miscellaneous case. Being aggrieved by said order dated 3-4-2023 the appellants has preferred this miscellaneous appeal which was duly admitted for hearing. 

 5. Mr. Amit Das Gupta, learned Advocate appearing for the appellants in the appeal and petitioners in the Civil Rule submits that in view of the provision under section 141 of the Code of Civil Procedure the Court of appeal should have fixed the miscellaneous case for taking evidence to give the appellants an opportunity to prove their case. Learned Advocate further submits that appellant No. 1 was tadbirkar on behalf of all appellants but he became seriously ill and bedridden and after some recovery he learnt about the dismissal of the appeal on 25-3-2020 but he could not file miscellaneous case in time due to loadown of civil courts for COVID-19 pandemic. Learned Advocate further submits that when the Courts reopened, the appellants filed the miscellaneous case on 6-7-2020 but the Court of appeal without taking into consideration of the above facts illegally dismissed the miscellaneous case. Learned Advocate further submits that the appeal was dismissed for default as the learned Advocate for the appellants did not take any steps for hearing of the appeal and for the fault of the learned Advocate, the appellants should not be suffered. Learned Advocate finally submits that the appellants should be given an opportunity to prove the miscellaneous case by adducing evidence for ends of justice. In support of his contention learned Advocate has referred to the cases of Mrinal Kanti Guha and others vs Brajendra Lal Dhar and others 44 DLR (AD) 9, Nahida Sultana vs Bazlur Rahman Khan and others 65 DLR 134 and Lajpat Rai and others vs State of Punjab and others AIR 1981 (SC) 1401. 

 6. Mr. Rafiqul Islam, learned Advocate appearing with Ms. Rasida Chowdhury, learned Advocate for respondent-opposite party Nos. 1-4 submits that the appellants could not sufficiently explain the cause of delay of 307 days in filing the miscellaneous case and, as such, the Court of appeal committed no illegality in dismissing the miscellaneous case and accordingly, interference is not called for by this Court. Learned Advocate further submits that in the meantime, the trial Court passed final decree and, as such, there is no scope to reopen the preliminary decree even after hearing the appeal on merit. 

 7. I have heard the learned Advocates, perused the memorandum of appeal, the impugned order, application filed under Order XLI, rule 19 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the application filed under section 5 of the Limitation Act and other materials available on record. The appellants contended that appellant No. 1 was the tadbirkar of the appeal and he became seriously ill and bedridden and though he learnt about the dismissal of the appeal on 25-3-2020 but could not file the miscellaneous case in time. In the application for condonation of delay it has been contended that due to COVID-19 pandemic all Courts were closed and as and when the Courts reopened the miscellaneous case has been filed. Respondent Nos. 1-4 filed written objection to contest the miscellaneous case claiming that the appellants made false statements in regards explaining the cause of delay. Thus whether the appellants were prevented by sufficient cause or not became disputed question of fact before the appellate Court and accordingly, the Court of appeal should have fixed date for taking evidence of the parties to resolve the issue. 

 8. Section 141 of the Code of Civil Procedure stipulates that the procedure provided in the code in regard to suit shall be followed as far as it can be made applicable in all proceedings in any Court of civil jurisdiction. Since this is a miscellaneous proceeding it comes within the definition of section 141 of the Code of Civil Procedure and accordingly, the Court of appeal should have followed the provision of section 141 of the Code and fixed date for taking evidence of the parties and disposed of the case on merit. 

 9. On perusal of the impugned order it appears that the Court of appeal, upon misconception of law and by giving some irrelevant findings dismissed the miscellaneous case and, as such, interference is called for by this Court. 

 12. Miscellaneous Case No. 1 of 2020 is restored to its original file and number. The learned Divisional Special Judge, Barishal is directed to dispose of the miscellaneous case being No. 1 of 2020 by giving opportunity to the parties to adduce evidence in support of their respective case and dispose of the same preferably within 3 (three) months from the date of receipt of the copy of this judgment. 

 14. The parties are directed to maintain status quo in respect of possession of the suit property till disposal of the miscellaneous case.
